NORM NELSON
One of stock car racing's most skillful drivers and
certainly the outstanding one to come from Wisconsin is
39 year old Norm Nelson of Racine. Nelson, winner of
four major stock car racing events at state fair park, has
scored more than 5,000 national championship late model
stock car points in the past 10 seasons. Nelson's career
dates back to 1942 when he purchased a V8 powered
midget from Jim Chandler, Racine.
Nelson raced midgets through 1948 with great success
although he was uneasy in some of the cars because he
found it difficult to fold his six foot, two inch frame into
the small cars. When the first stock car race as held at
state fair park Aug. 22, 1948, Nelson finished fourth in a
1946 Ford. That started him off on his career as a stock
car driver. Nelson also took a whirl at the hot rods in
the 1949 season, winning a couple of features and setting
several track records along the way.
Except for rides in a Ford and Mercury, Nelson used
Oldsmobiles in all of the races in which he competed from
1948 through 1954. In 1955, Nelson drove one of the three
1955 Chrysler 300s, teamed with Tony Bettenhausen and
Frank Mundy. He won the July 17 race that year. He
crashed into the south turn wall after blowing a right
front tire right after receiving the checker flag. Unhurt,
Nelson walked back to the starting line to claim the win-

TROUBLE IN THE TURN
30
30
Max Winter Photos, Courtesy Midwest Racing News
Things were going along smoothly in the Aug, 23, 1959 150 mile late model stock car race here when
Iggy Katona, Lambertville, Mich. (#30 - 1958 Ford) spun midway through the south turn. Katona's car skid-
ded up to the outer wall just in time to be met head on by Billy Shoulders, Waukegan, Ill. (#15 - 1958 Olds 88).
Result? Two bent front ends and wrinkled hoods. But Iggy's troubles were far from over. Carl "Red"
Swanberg, Carpentersville, Ill. (#10 - 1957 Chevrolet) sideswiped Katona's car washing out the right front side
of Swanberg's car as well. Nobody was injured and all three cars were hauled off. The yellow flag was out
from the 58th to 67th miles and when things got going again, Rodger Ward won the race. Swanberg and
Shoulders both came back for the 200 miler the following Thursday but rain stopped the show. Iggy ap-
parently had enough. He didn't come back.
